description:
`cargo-ci.sh` records a step that failed because the disk was full as a verdict on repository content, so digest reuse replays the failure until a forced rerun. This makes an out-of-space failure environment-sensitive.

## Background

`scripts/cargo-ci.sh` exits 1 for a verdict and 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL, recorded as an `error` gate run and never reused through digest reuse) when every failing step is environment-sensitive and the host was loaded. Its header lists the environment-sensitive cases: a `test` step with nextest TIMEOUT results and no FAIL or ABORT, and a `budget` step whose only violation is the suite-duration budget. On this host `/tmp` is a shared tmpfs, and under parallel CI it fills: tests then fail with "No space left on device" (os error 28), for example `profile_cli_tests::test_profile_pack_and_add_carry_a_package_at_the_model_limits`, and the run is classified as exit 1. The `cargo-ci` gate description in `.jit/gates.toml` restates the classification and is projected into `docs/reference/rules-and-gates.md`. `scripts/cargo-ci-selftest.sh` owns the classifier's behaviour.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A run in which a failing step's output reports ENOSPC ("No space left on device" or os error 28) exits 75 whatever the load baseline, and its message names ENOSPC as the cause.
- [hard] REQ-02: A run whose failing steps include a failure not caused by ENOSPC, or any other verdict step, still exits 1.
- [hard] REQ-03: The exit-code header of `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` and the `cargo-ci` gate description in `.jit/gates.toml` list ENOSPC as environment-sensitive, and the generated rules-and-gates projection is re-rendered.
- [hard] REQ-04: `scripts/cargo-ci-selftest.sh` covers both cases: a step failing only with ENOSPC exits 75, and an ENOSPC failure alongside a genuine test FAIL exits 1.

## Notes

Steward request (2026-11-04). Lands before f487aeef, which also edits `cargo-ci.sh`'s classification header.
title: cargo-ci classifies out-of-space failures as environment faults
